title: recording 1.0.0
description: Each trial recording that completeness reports as present is a usable MCAP file. It opens and has a valid footer and summary. Every required channel exists and has messages. Message timestamps never go backwards on a channel. No gap between consecutive messages on a channel is longer than the declared limit. Gaps are measured in log-time order: the messages on a channel are ordered by log time before the gaps are taken, so a write that is out of file order is not a capture gap. Timestamps that go backwards are counted in file order and are reported as timestamps-backwards. The file's size and sha256 match media.json, and the observation_sha256 in media.json matches the run evidence. A file that is not complete is reported once, as mcap-incomplete, and its channels are not also reported as missing-channel, so the cause reads clearly. A recording that completeness reports as missing, truncated, or empty is not judged here and is listed in not_checked with reason not-present. A present recording the evidence has no entry for is listed with reason not-recorded. not_checked is optional. Without media the check is not applicable. percentage is 100 times the number of judged recordings without a finding divided by the number of judged recordings. The check judges structure, channels, and time. It does not judge what the recorded motion means. The reader reports the channel facts, and the check compares them with the declared channels and limit. The result states the gap limit it used in limits.max_gap_seconds, equal to evidence.recording.max_gap_seconds, whenever the check is applicable. limits is omitted when the check is not applicable. Evidence for this check is evidence.recording.

media_available.description: False when the run has no media job output, so there are no recordings or media.json to read.

max_gap_seconds.description: The longest allowed gap between consecutive messages on a channel.

state.description: incomplete means the file does not open or has no valid footer and summary.

backward_steps.description: The number of messages whose log time is earlier than the message before it on the channel, in file order.

max_gap_seconds.description: The longest gap between consecutive messages on the channel, in log-time order.
